item.title: GovBrief Today #650
item.description: An Army sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier told Pete Hegseth’s group to be quiet today. It was Veterans Day in a country at war, and Donald Trump had already left the wreath-laying ceremony. The plaza at the tomb was empty except for the soldier on guard. Hegseth stayed on the steps above it and posed arm in arm with his wife and two others for a photographer. Then he waved more of his aides down and they lined up for a second picture. The laughing started as that second group broke up. “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times,” the soldier called out. A day earlier, nine members of the Kennedy family had asked a federal judge to stop Trump’s 250-foot arch because its shadow would fall on their relatives’ graves in that same cemetery. Two of them called it hallowed ground. For Pete Hegseth, his wife, and his aides, it was a backdrop. I’ve emailed 9,899 stories over 650 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can’t show them all to you. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I will. NEW: Zoom In is now live! item.title: Christopher judge says he doesn’t understand why shows based on successful games don’t bring back the original actors and writers
item.description: Christopher Judge believes Hollywood should involve more of the original actors and writers when adapting successful video games 00 Although he had praise for Pedro Pascal's performance in The Last of Us, he questioned why the game cast was not used for scenes that were recreated so closely. Judge also criticised Amazon's God of War series for leaving out writers from the games, saying, "These guys have been immersed in this world for 20 years. But someone's going to know better?"
